# Tjinimin walks into a environmental & climate services firm

Walk into any environmental & climate services outfit and watch for ten minutes. You will see a very old act performed with newer props. The act has a name. It is **Tjinimin**.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Quarrel with Kunmanggur.** Tjinimin quarrelled with Kunmanggur, the great Rainbow Serpent.  He desired Kunmanggur's consorts, the Green Parrot-Girls, and sought to take them for himself.  The dispute set the ancestral being against the authority of the Rainbow Serpent, testing the limits of proper relationship and social order.

**The Vow beneath the Stars.** Defeated in the quarrel, Tjinimin hung himself upside down in a tree.  There he gazed at the stars and made a solemn vow: he would never have sex again.  The posture of suspension and the vow of abstinence mark a radical withdrawal from the social and reproductive world.

## Not the First Rebrand

Tjinimin belongs specifically to Murrinh-Patha tradition rather than to the wider cross-cultural networks of the Kimberley Wandjina or Arnhem Land Rainbow Serpent complexes.  Within Murrinh-Patha cosmology he is grouped with the ancestor-figures whose stories encode law, kinship, and the origins of animal species. The office is only the latest translation.
